gemini-2.5-flash.standardized_narrative: In 2017, Syndicate 1729 experienced an overall strengthening of GBP 1.8 million in prior year reserves. This adverse development was primarily attributed to a reduction in premium on the casualty reinsurance class of business. The 2015 year of account closed with a loss, although a material US Casualty contract commutation provided some relief. The 2016 year of account also saw adverse loss experience in Property Insurance, partly due to the impact of Hurricanes Harvey, Irma, and Maria, with 15% of their total net exposure affecting this year. A similar US Casualty contract commutation also benefited the 2016 year.

gpt-5-mini.standardized_narrative: Opening gross claims outstanding at 1 Jan 2017 were GBP 54.925m. During 2017 the Syndicate recorded an overall adverse prior-year development (deficit) of GBP 1.8m (c.3.28% of opening gross claims), described as primarily generated by a reduction in premium on the casualty reinsurance class of business. Separately, 2017 experienced significant natural catastrophe activity (Hurricanes Harvey, Irma, Maria and US wildfires) which produced material 2017-year claims; the Syndicate estimated a combined net exposure to those 2017 cat events of $10.4m. The prior-year deterioration is therefore small relative to the current year catastrophe impact and has been attributed to adverse development in casualty/reinsurance business.
